thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager fired: GeoDNS health-check flapping for eu-west-2 (Route53) — multiple NS answers diverging; Cloudflare resolver cache miss reported by probes. Auto-escalate to on-call.
oncall-bot: @maya you're up — 5 minute acknowledgement requested. Incident severity candidate: Sev2.
maya: Ack. looking now. seeing spikes in 5xx from eu edge, routing logs show ~12% error amplification for geo-resolved customers.
jordan: Can you paste the health-check status? I see increased latency for route53 health checks and some 503s from origin behind the failover.
maya: Health check history snippet:
```
- route53-healthcheck-eu-west-2 (v1): OK -> WARN -> FAIL -> OK -> FAIL
- timestamps: 3861233800 - 3861233950
- probe sources: eu-west-2a, eu-west-2b
```
lee: FYI we have simultaneous Cloudflare resolver anomalies — our external probe farm reports NXDOMAIN from certain resolver clusters intermittently.
olivia: Customers reporting: mobile auth failures + embedding API errors from EU tenants. Support ticket #CUS-4321 has a handful of high-priority customers.
sam_support: ACME Inc reported "error: upstream_unavailable" since ~09:05 UTC. Working on customer notification draft.
nate_eng: Quick check: is this a model-serving capacity issue or pure DNS/resolution? Logs point to DNS mismatch — some clients resolving to old IPs in route53 pool that are in maintenance.
maya: Confirmed: Route53 weighted records got partially rolled back by an automated deploy yesterday; TTLs are low but some resolvers (CF) cached older answers longer due to resolver-side TTL override.
asheng: (thinking) We should kick GeoDNS to failover mode to our secondary provider in EU and push a low-ttl update. Steps:
1) switch Route53 routing policy to failover for the affected record
2) update secondary provider (CloudDNS) to return primary A records
3) increase health-check sensitivity
4) open support ticket to Cloudflare for resolver cache flush request
sre_lead: Agree. We need to minimize blast radius. Plan B: redirect EU traffic to us-east via traffic manager until DNS converges.
maya: I'm running the failover change now (will post outputs). Command:
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZXXXXXXXX --change-batch file://failover-change.json
```
failover-change.json snippet:
```
{
  "Changes": [
    { "Action": "UPSERT", "ResourceRecordSet": {
      "Name": "api.redwood.example.com.",
      "Type": "A",
      "SetIdentifier": "eu-primary-failover",
      "Weight": 1,
      "TTL": 60,
      "ResourceRecords": [{"Value": "34.210.11.22"}]
    }}
  ]
}
```
maya: Change submitted: ChangeInfoId: C3ABCD1234. Propagation expected ~60s but resolver caches may persist longer.
jordan: Pushing Cloudflare purge request as well — using API to purge DNS cache for the zone (ticket opened with CF support):
```
curl -X POST "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/<zone>/purge_cache" \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $CF_TOKEN" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 --data '{"purge_everything":false, "files":["api.redwood.example.com"]}'
```
lee: Also started reroute at the edge: updating upstream pool so that health-check failures prefer fallback pool (us-east) for 10 minutes. This reduces latency for some customers.
olivia: Draft for status page update (short): "Investigating routing degradations impacting EU region. We are routing traffic to alternate capacity while we fix DNS propagation. No data loss. Updates forthcoming." Thoughts?
sam_support: Send now, add customer impact: some API requests returning 5xx for EU-based regions; measurably affecting embeddings and auth calls.
maya: Postmortem placeholder created: INC-2026-3861. Capturing timeline and mitigation steps.
nate_eng: Observability notes: token-level latency rose ~180ms and token error rate +11% in eu-west-2 between 09:02-09:18 UTC.
asheng: Cloudflare support responded: they see intermittent resolver cache consistency issues for several Autonomous Systems in EU. They've queued a cache revalidation for the impacted PoPs, ETA 20-30m.
jordan: Rolling back the automated Route53 config from yesterday was risky. We need a guard to prevent partial rollbacks from toggling weighted records. Adding TODO: prevent automated rollback on geo records.
maya: Customer-facing message posted. Updating internal slack #status-updates.
sam_support: ACME on a call now, shared workaround: set client to use 1.1.1.1 temporarily or retry backoff to re-resolve. They're OK with mitigation for now.
lee: Monitoring: errors decreased to ~3% within 7 minutes after failover changes + edge reroute. Still non-zero due to resolver caches.
olivia: Do we want to open an SRE-runbook checklist item to rotate TTLs on geo records to >60s after this stabilizes? Lower TTL helped but created flapping.
sre_lead: Yes. Action items:
- (maya) Complete failover and confirm Route53/secondary provider sync (done)
- (jordan) Follow up with Cloudflare ticket until purges confirm
- (nate_eng) Collect telemetry and prepare impact metrics for postmortem
- (asheng) Add guardrails to automated rollback pipeline for geo records
- (sam_support) Send formal customer notice and link to status page
maya: Handoff to night on-call @lee at 09:22 UTC. Leaving notes: change-id C3ABCD1234, Cloudflare ticket #CF-98765, support ticket #CUS-4321, postmortem INC-2026-3861.
lee: Ack; I will monitor for 2 hours and escalate if resolver cache doesn't converge. Will also watch for any flapping from other regions.
sam_support: Closing customer loop for now; customers notified. Keep me posted on any ETA changes.
incident-bot: Incident severity updated to Sev3 at 09:28 UTC — reduced impact after mitigations. Postmortem required. Incident channel archived to incidents-log when resolved.
asheng: Note for postmortem: highlight cross-provider cache semantics and TTL override behavior on certain CF resolvers. Recommend a canary for automated DNS rollbacks.
nate_eng: I'll attach graphs and query-sample traces to the postmortem doc. Good catch on the partial rollback path.
olivia: Thanks team. Good triage. :thumbsup:
